title: Texas's 25th Congressional District election, 2026
description: The 2026 election for Texas's 25th Congressional District pits incumbent Republican Congressman Roger Williams against Democratic challenger Dione Sims. The district spans from Tarrant County in the east to Callahan County in the west, covering 13 counties in north-central Texas including parts of Fort Worth and surrounding rural areas. The race takes place under new congressional maps passed by the Texas Legislature in August 2025 and upheld by the U.S. Supreme Court, which have made the district somewhat more competitive. Cook Political Report rates this race as Solidly Republican, but Sims, the granddaughter of Juneteenth activist Dr. Opal Lee, has drawn attention as a Democratic challenger seeking to flip the seat.
polling_note: No district-specific general election polls were found for TX-25 in 2026. The Cook Political Report rates the race as Solidly Republican.

candidates.name: Roger Williams
candidates.summary: Roger Williams has represented Texas's 25th Congressional District since 2013. He is a former Texas Secretary of State (2004-2007), a businessman who owned car dealerships, and a former minor league baseball player and college baseball coach at Texas Christian University (TCU). Williams chairs the House Committee on Small Business and has focused on tax reform, regulatory relief, and veterans' issues.

candidates.name: Dione Sims
candidates.summary: Dione Sims is the Democratic nominee for Texas's 25th Congressional District, having won the March 3, 2026 primary. She is the granddaughter of Dr. Opal Lee, the activist known as the 'Grandmother of Juneteenth,' and serves as President and Founder of Unity Unlimited, Inc., which produces the annual Juneteenth Fort Worth Celebration. Sims has worked as a community advocate and was involved in efforts to establish the National Juneteenth Museum and advance Juneteenth education in Texas schools.

forecast.rationale: No district-specific general election polls were found. The non-polling signals point strongly toward the Republican incumbent: Roger Williams has held the seat since 2013, chairs the House Small Business Committee, and the Cook Political Report rates the race as Solidly Republican. However, the newly enacted 2025 maps are described as 'somewhat more competitive,' and the complete absence of polling data elevates uncertainty. Dione Sims, the Democratic challenger, has a notable public profile as Dr. Opal Lee's granddaughter and a Juneteenth advocate, but no polling quantifies her support. The rating stops at likely_r (rather than safe_r) to reflect the map changes and sparse data, yielding roughly a 93% Republican win probability with low confidence.
